cot_history.reasoning_cot: I can only react to opponents’ immediate previous bids. If any opponent previously bid aggressively near/above my daily salary, I match a strong bid to prevent them from outbidding and forcing my no-water days up. Otherwise, I bid moderately to secure enough water while preserving budget.

Yesterday Cindy paid very high bids (~134.8 avg) and survived; Alex bid moderately; Eric also bid high. This suggests aggressive competition for scarce water. To win reliably, bid around a strong but not max level when supply is mid/high, and conserve budget when supply is lower or my hp is low.

Yesterday Eric died quickly (hp->0 by day 4) while bidding very low (~29). Others survived full 10 days with high bids (~96-118). So use a mid bid to avoid being outbid by strong survivors, but don’t overpay since no one else collapsed; scale down when supply is tight.

Yesterday, Cindy outbid heavily (~94 avg) and survived all 10 days, while Alex/Eric show extreme bidding volatility. To avoid overpaying, we anchor a mid-high bid that should beat Cindy when supply is only 15-25, but we scale down if our hp is low or budget is tight.

With our low requirement (9) and likely moderate supply (15–25), we can bid midrange to secure enough water while preserving budget. We react to yesterday’s max bid: if others are bidding aggressively, we slightly undercut; if not, we bid comfortably above a baseline.

To exploit, keep our bids mid-high when supply is ample, but avoid overpaying if our HP is low; otherwise bid just above likely competitive level.

To avoid overpaying, bid moderately when supply is near mid, but spike if supply is low or if any rival bid near/above 70.
